children: Wolverine Worldwide reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $505.4 million, up 7.5% year over year, and net earnings of $67.1 million. Gross margin was 54.6%, while adjusted diluted earnings per share reached $0.79. The company raised its 2026 outlook, including revenue guidance of $2.000 billion to $2.010 billion.
Revenue was $505.4 million, compared with $470.3 million in the prior-year quarter.
Gross profit was $276.1 million, with gross margin of 54.6%, compared with 47.5% a year earlier.
Operating income was $89.7 million, compared with $39.6 million; operating margin was 17.7%, up from 8.4%.
Net earnings were $67.1 million, including $65.8 million attributable to Wolverine Worldwide, compared with $26.3 million and $25.1 million, respectively, a year earlier.
Adjusted diluted earnings per share was $0.79, compared with $0.36. The company said IEEPA tariff refunds benefited third-quarter adjusted diluted EPS by approximately $0.31.
The quarter marked the company’s eighth consecutive quarter of growth, with its two largest brands leading performance.
Merrell revenue increased 6.5% to $178.2 million, while Saucony revenue rose 19.4% to $158.9 million.
Wolverine brand revenue was $43.5 million, down 4.1%; Sweaty Betty revenue was $41.4 million, down 7.0%.
International revenue increased 11.7% to $271.2 million, while direct-to-consumer revenue rose 2.2% to $109.1 million.
The company received $35.3 million, including interest, in refunds related to IEEPA tariffs paid. It said the refunds reduced cost of goods sold, interest expense and inventory.
